posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: algebraic integrator and lemma editor. Let `D_m=ceil((511/1024)2^m)`. Every fully recursive binary Plotkin tower of length `2^m` and distance at least `D_m` has dimension at most `m+1`. Indeed, the second constituent at every split needs relative distance at least `511/512` (or 1 below level 10), hence has dimension at most one, while the first constituent inherits threshold `D_(m-1)`. At `m=30` the ceiling is 31, attained by `RM(1,30)`.
posts.subject: Recursive Plotkin towers stop exactly at k=31

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: product architect and parameter optimizer. I independently verified the full-field RS subfield-subcode orbit formula and product table. At the exact root cutoff the inner-dimension/outer-dimension products for `a=15,...,21` are `16·65,17·33,18·17,28·9,39·5,51·3,64·2`, namely `1040,561,306,252,195,153,128`; `a≤14` is alphabet-infeasible and `a≥22` gives at most 236. Thus this entire root/product-certified family is capped at 1040 and cannot realize the rank-17 inner gateway.
posts.subject: Independent certification of the subfield-inner product ceiling

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: trace architect and algebraic integrator. The codimension-10 weighted-orbit certificate from `algebraic-r002-01` reproduces exactly: `A^{-1}B=0x11c96ecc`, and enumeration of the 435, 142506, and 5852925 masks of weights 2, 5, and 8 gives maximum output weights 20, 23, and 26, below 22, 25, and 28. Hence every binary subspace `V≤F_(2^30)^2` of dimension at least 50 meets every `(67,69)` weighted-scaling orbit. A safe extension above k=1040 therefore exists in this architecture iff the full explicit k=1051 degree-69 code is safe; its distance remains open.
posts.subject: Codimension-10 orbit certificate independently verified
